stem: Who gave the theory of gravity?
expl: In 1687, Isaac Newton published his law of gravitation in his book "Mathematical Principles of Natural Philosophy". stem: If the spinning speed of the Earth increases, then the weight of the body at the equator will :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The weight of a body on the Earth is the amount of gravitational pull on it exerted by the Earth. Due to Earth's rotation, centrifugal force also exerted on a body on Earth, which tries to move the body away from the centre of the Earth. At the equator, centrifugal force is maximum as the velocity of rotation is maximum at the equator of the Earth. Thus, at the equator, centrifugal force acts against gravity to reduce the weight of the body. With the increase in the speed of rotation of the Earth, the centrifugal force at equator will increase and the weight of the body will seem to have decreased.

stem: Weightlessness is –

When your body is effectively in 'free fall', accelerating downwards at the acceleration of gravity, then you are not being supported. The sensation of apparent weight comes from the support that you feel from the floor, from the seat etc. The term 'zero gravity' is often used to describe such condition.

stem: The Earth travels in its orbit at a speed of approx 4,400 km per hour. Why do we not feel this high speed ?

options.label: c
options.text: The solar system as a whole is also moving.

options.label: d
options.text: The gravity of the Earth constantly pulls us towards the Earth’s centre.

expl: The Earth spins and moves through space in an orbit around the sun. We don’t 'feel' this movement because we are spinning and moving through space with the Earth. Since we are standing on the Earth, we move as much (and as fast) as the Earth moves. One way to recognize the Earth’s movement is to look at objects that are not attached to Earth , like the Sun or stars. For example, if we are in a car which is moving at a constant speed on a smooth surface, we will not feel its motion. However, when the car accelerates or when the brakes are applied, we do feel the motion.

stem:
Consider the following statements : A Simple Pendulum is set into oscillation Then :
1. the acceleration is zero when the bob passes through the mean position.
2. in each cycle the bob attains a given velocity twice.
3. both acceleration and velocity of the bob are zero when it reaches its extreme position during the oscillation.
4. the amplitude of oscillation of the simple pendulum decreases with time.
Which of these statements are correct ?
expl: When an object, which is in simple harmonic motion passes through its mean position, then (i) No force acts on it. (ii) Its acceleration becomes zero. (iii) It has maximum velocity. (iv) It has maximum kinetic energy. (v) Its potential energy is zero. When the object reaches its extreme position then, (i) Its acceleration is maximum. (ii) Counterforce acting on it is maximum. (iii) Its Kinetic energy is zero. (iv) It has maximum potential energy. (v) It has zero velocity. In each rotation, the pendulum twice attains a specific velocity. In addition, under normal circumstances oscillation of usual pendulum decreases with time (due to air resistance etc.). Thus the statement 1, 2 and 4 are correct while statement 3 is wrong.

stem:
Given below are two statements–
Assertion (A) : Lighting a candle in space does not produce a flame.
Reason (R) : A flame exists due to the pull of gravity. In the context of above, which one of the following is correct?

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: b
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation.

expl: NASA made it clear by his experiment that gravitation is must for lighting up a candle. In the case of microgravity in the spacecraft, we are able to light up the flame but it is not possible in an actual vacuum. In fact, the flickering frequency of a flame is proportional to the square root of the acceleration due to gravity to the diameter of the candle and due to the lack of gravitational force in space, it is zero. Thus, the correct Answer is (a).
